title: What a Finite Expected Spectrum Can Identify
shortTitle: What a finite expected spectrum can identify
oneLine: A finite expected site-frequency spectrum observes only finitely many exponential projections; this corrected candidate proves why sharp calendar-window targets can remain unidentified and supplies an exact positive collision.
abstract: Under the stated neutral, single-population Kingman and infinite-sites assumptions, a finite unfolded expected site-frequency spectrum observes a finite span of exponential coalescence kernels. This unrefereed candidate proves that a sharp calendar-window mean, or a ratio of two distinct window means, is not identified over a declared broad positive history class. The proof accounts for the history-dependent inverse map from coalescent time to calendar time. An explicit three-haplotype construction gives two strictly positive histories with exactly the same unfolded and folded expected spectra but calendar-window ratios 0.4411819836 and 1.7935760644. The package also characterises the linear functionals retained after folding, separates exact fibre statements from first-order Gaussian information, and proposes a covariance-aware empirical design. A formula-first priority audit materially narrows the originality claim: Myers, Fefferman and Patterson already establish calendar/genetic-time separation, positive same-spectrum histories and exponential projection structure; Bhaskar and Song supply finite Laplace coordinates, the SFS bridge, scale equivalence and folded parity. The release is therefore offered as a target-specific sharp-window formalisation, explicit witness and integrated assurance package, not as the first discovery of demographic non-identifiability. It does not establish equality of linked genomic laws or adjudicate the proposed 813–930 ka human bottleneck.
narration: A site-frequency spectrum is a compact histogram of genetic variation. Even if its expected values were known without sampling error, it would still reveal only finitely many exponential averages of population history. This corrected release asks a sharper question: can those averages determine the mean population size inside a fixed calendar-time window? Under a neutral one-population coalescent model and a broad positive class of histories, the answer is no. Calendar time must be recomputed separately for every candidate history. The package gives two strictly positive histories with exactly the same finite expected spectrum, but their ratios for the same illustrative calendar windows are about zero point four four one and one point seven nine four. One implies a depression; the other implies an expansion. Folding the spectrum loses further coordinates, and the paper characterises the bounded linear functionals that remain identifiable. The priority audit also corrects the earlier framing. Myers, Fefferman and Patterson already established broad same-spectrum ambiguity, calendar versus genetic time and exponential projections. Bhaskar and Song supplied the finite Laplace coordinates and folded parity. This release therefore claims a target-specific sharp-window synthesis, explicit witness and replayable assurance package, not first discovery. The result concerns an exact expected summary. It does not establish equality of linked genomic laws, decide the ancient human bottleneck, or substitute producer replay for independent reproduction, specialist review or peer review.

problem.name: Target-specific identifiability from a finite expected site-frequency spectrum

keyResults: Under the stated neutral one-population Kingman, infinite-sites, fixed-scale and common-known-tail model, no finite exact expected SFS identifies a sharp calendar-window mean or a ratio of two distinct window means over the declared broad positive history class.

An explicit n=3 pair of strictly positive histories has the same exact unfolded and folded expected SFS but calendar-window ratios 0.4411819836 and 1.7935760644 for the same dimensionless illustrative windows.

The exact unnormalised folded expected SFS is equivalent to the even coalescence moments; for essentially bounded weights, its identified linear functionals are exactly the corresponding even-kernel span.

Known linear compression cannot increase first-order regular target information in the stated fixed-covariance Gaussian tangent experiment; this first-order result is not promoted to an exact nonlinear equivalence.

A formula-first audit records direct prior-art collisions for broad demographic ambiguity, calendar/genetic-time separation, exponential projection structure and finite Laplace coordinates. The target-specific sharp-window package is a bridge-level synthesis, not a first-discovery claim.
evidence: A 22-page anonymous candidate paper and accessible Markdown source; machine-readable claim and priority targets; primary-source citation audit; exact calendar and folded receipts; two same-producer SFS-forward routes; 120 deterministic tests; 11 hostile controls plus one clean comparison; ordinary and optimized Python replay; a byte-reproducible PDF build; a 72-file SHA-256 inventory; frozen reviews and responses; and fresh-extraction verification from the tagged commit. These checks establish bounded producer-side internal consistency and artifact identity, not theorem truth, independent reproduction, specialist acceptance, priority or impact.

It does not adjudicate the proposed ancient human bottleneck.
